title: Props
summary: Props (short for properties) are read-only data passed from a parent component to a child component. They customize a component's output, much like HTML attributes. Props flow one way — parent to child (unidirectional data flow). A component should never modify its own props. Destructuring props in the function parameter is the standard pattern.
keyPoints: Props are passed as attributes: <MovieCard title='Inception' rating={8.8} />
Access props by destructuring the parameter: function MovieCard({ title, rating })
Props are read-only — a component must never modify its own props
Data flows one way: parent → child (unidirectional data flow)
Pass any JavaScript value: strings, numbers, arrays, objects, functions
Default values: function MovieCard({ rating = 0 }) — used when the prop is not passed
The special children prop contains whatever is nested between opening and closing tags

exercises.prompt: How do you pass a title prop to a MovieCard component?
exercises.explanation: Props are passed as attributes in JSX, just like HTML attributes. The component receives them as properties of its props object.

exercises.prompt: Which correctly receives and uses the title prop?
exercises.explanation: Props arrive as a single object. Destructuring { title } extracts the property. Without destructuring, you'd write (props) and access props.title.

exercises.prompt: What does 'unidirectional data flow' mean in React?
options: Data flows from child components up to parent components
Data flows from parent components down to child components via props
Data can only flow between sibling components
Data flows in both directions between parent and child
exercises.answer: Data flows from parent components down to child components via props
exercises.explanation: React enforces a one-way data flow: parents pass data to children through props. Children cannot directly modify parent data — they use callbacks instead.

exercises.answer: The local variable changes but it violates the props contract — props should be treated as read-only
exercises.explanation: Reassigning a destructured variable works in JavaScript, but it breaks React's mental model. Props are meant to be read-only. Use state if you need mutable data.

exercises.prompt: How do you pass a number and a function as props?
exercises.explanation: Non-string values must be passed inside curly braces {}. Strings can use quotes, but numbers, functions, arrays, and objects require braces.

Title

Body
options: The JSX elements nested between <Card> and </Card>

exercises.answer: The JSX elements nested between <Card> and </Card>
exercises.explanation: Anything between a component's opening and closing tags is passed as the special children prop. The Card component can render it with {children}.

exercises.explanation: Default parameter values in destructuring are used when the prop is undefined (not passed or explicitly set to undefined).
